title: Svelte Practice
description: Practise the twelve ideas in this Svelte course. Choose an answer, then read why it fits the example.

exercises.question: What does {club} insert?
options: The whole script as visible text
exercises.explanation: A Svelte component can contain a script and page markup. Curly brackets show a JavaScript value in the markup.

exercises.question: Which rune makes count reactive?
exercises.explanation: The $state rune creates a value Svelte tracks. Changing it can update the part of the page that reads it.

exercises.question: What makes pages update?
options: The books value it depends on changes
exercises.explanation: The $derived rune describes a value calculated from other state. It stays connected to the values it uses.

exercises.question: Which message appears when ready is false?
exercises.explanation: An if block includes content only when its condition is true. Its else part handles the other case.

exercises.question: What does (book.id) provide?
options: A key for the repeated item
exercises.explanation: An each block repeats markup for a list. A key identifies each item even when its position changes.

exercises.question: What does bind:value connect?
options: The input and a remote database
The input value and name state
exercises.explanation: bind:value links an input to a state value. Typing changes that state and the parts of the page that read it.

exercises.question: Which rune reads component props?
exercises.explanation: A prop is a value given to a component by its parent. $props reads those inputs in Svelte 5.

exercises.question: Who decides what happens after the callback?
options: The parent that supplies the function
exercises.explanation: A callback prop lets a child ask its parent to react. The parent decides what to do with the supplied value.

exercises.question: What does {@render children?.()} do?
options: Renders the supplied children snippet if it exists
exercises.explanation: A snippet is a reusable piece of Svelte markup. A children snippet lets a wrapper render content supplied by its parent.

exercises.question: Which tool is better for a calculated total?
options: An effect that repeatedly writes the total
exercises.explanation: An effect runs after Svelte updates the page and tracks reactive values it reads. Its returned function cleans up work before rerun or removal.

exercises.question: Why scope component CSS?
options: To reduce unintended changes to other components
To stop all CSS from being created
exercises.explanation: Svelte scopes ordinary component styles so they mainly affect markup from that component. This helps avoid accidental changes elsewhere.

exercises.question: Why check title.trim()?
options: To avoid adding an empty or space-only title
exercises.explanation: A form can add trimmed text to a reactive list. Handling submit supports both the button and the Enter key.
